name: BuildParty deterministic workflow
description: Production-parity BuildParty evaluation. Public native surface is exactly eleven WebMCP operations. human_fixture_add_feedback models the production human-only comment route; eval_full_journey is composite supporting infrastructure required by the v1 single-action harness. Production uses PostgreSQL transactions, authenticated bearer capabilities/participant tokens, generated UUIDs/timestamps, and rendered portable HTML; this bundle uses deterministic authoritative fixtures while preserving lifecycle, role, attribution, linkage, zero-to-200-block, version, body-only response, complete revision snapshot, archive/re-anchor, pruning, and immutability semantics. Final HTML is a deterministic self-contained sandbox export derived only from finalized block source and shared state.

tools.title: Initialize agent
tools.description: Call this first when the user asks to use or start BuildParty. On landing, store a reusable agent display identity (use Owner if none is useful); on a party page, create or reuse that party's participant session. Then follow nextAction.

tools.title: Create party
tools.description: After init on the landing page, create exactly one review room (use title BuildParty session when no supplied content suggests one). Returns the only portable capability results: private owner URL and reviewer URL; continue in the opened party instead of creating another room.

tools.title: Get party
tools.description: Read first after init in an existing party, and before any versioned change. Returns current artifact, shared state, lifecycle, revisions, open-feedback count, available operations, and a deterministic next action.

tools.title: Set artifact
tools.description:
Publish prepared conversation content as the first artifact, or replace the whole artifact when get_party advertises this operation. Use stable blocks for independently reviewable sections. Required literals: artifact.format must be "buildparty.artifact/v1" and every block.kind must be "sandbox". source.html is required; CSS/JS are optional and must be self-contained/no-network. Simple text example: {"artifact":{"format":"buildparty.artifact/v1","title":"Note","blocks":[{"id":"note","kind":"sandbox","source":{"html":"

Hello

"}}]}}

tools.title: Update blocks
tools.description: After get_party, make targeted source edits to existing stable blocks or patch shared state at the exact current version. Link relevant feedbackIds to source edits; a statePatch-only update does not create a revision.

tools.title: Delete blocks
tools.description: Remove obsolete review sections and their shared state at the exact current version when advertised. Deleting every block deliberately leaves a valid zero-block artifact; it does not delete the artifact, room, or revision history.

tools.title: Restore revision
tools.description: Undo unwanted changes by restoring an available pre-final revision as the whole current artifact and shared state, creating a new revision. changedBlockIds may be empty when only title, format, or shared state changed.

tools.title: Get feedback
tools.description: Read human review comments and prior agent responses before revising. Use open status to find actionable active or archived feedback, then target source changes and link feedback IDs.

tools.title: Respond to feedback
tools.description: Acknowledge a comment or, after a targeted update_blocks call, link its returned revision and resolve the addressed feedback. Never claim resolution without that revision link.

tools.title: Finalize party
tools.description: Owner-only: when review is complete, lock the exact current version as immutable final output. Open active feedback requires an explicit allowOpenFeedback override; do not use it casually.

tools.title: Get final artifact
tools.description: After finalization, retrieve immutable final metadata and portable interactive HTML for delivery or download; this is read-only and cannot reopen editing.

tools.title: Human fixture: add feedback
tools.description: Evaluation-only deterministic human action corresponding to production add_feedback; supporting infrastructure, never native WebMCP.

tools.title: Evaluation full journey
tools.description: Evaluation-only composite supporting infrastructure for the v1 single-action harness; never native WebMCP. Public delete/restore behavior is exercised by dedicated one-action tasks.
